newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iraq's crude oil contract customers detailed.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's crude oil contract customers detailed.

text.p: Iraq's Oil Minister Muhammad Rasheed on Sunday said that Iraq had signed oil contracts with 11 firms under the United Nations approved "oil-for-food" deal.
The following companies have said they intend to lift Iraqi crude under U.N. guidelines.

Turkish state refiner Tupras Turkiye Petrol Rafinerileri has signed a 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) deal with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) from the Mediterranean coastal port of Ceyhan.
The first cargo under this contract and Iraq's first tanker export for six years is expected later Monday when the vessel Gole leaves Ceyhan carrying Kirkuk crude.

U.S. Coastal Corp has a 60,000 bpd contract which is expected to be delivered from the Mina al-Bakr terminal in the northern Gulf. The VLCC Star of Africa is currently being loaded and will depart by the end of this week.
U.S. independent Bayoil is currently loading the 272,000 deadweight tonne Leonidas vessel at Mina al Bakr, Gulf industry sources said on Monday.
Texaco Inc is in negotiations with SOMO for a contract to lift between 35,000 bpd and 40,000 bpd.
French firm Total SA said on Monday that it had signed a contract to lift 30,000 bpd of Iraqi oil providing the U.N. approved the agreement.
Elf Aquitaine is also understood to be in talks with SOMO.

Japan's Mitsubishi Corp signed an agreement on Friday to buy 40,000 bpd of crude. Industry sources said Mitsubishi is acting as an agent for five Japanese oil firms -- Japan Energy Corp, Nippon Oil, Kashima Oil Co, Showa Shell Sekiyu KK and Mitsubishi Oil Co ltd .
Marubeni Corp and Itochu Corp have also talked contract terms with SOMO in Baghdad this month.
Private Italian oil refiner Oil Energy has a 10,000 bpd contract covering three months.
Brazil's state oil firm Petrobras is negotiating a price formula with SOMO to buy between 20,000 bpd and 30,000 bpd.
London-based trading firm Trafigura has reached an agreement for 20,000 bpd of Kirkuk crude destined for Romania, the Cyprus-based Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter reported on Monday.
Other companies in talks with Iraq included Italy's Agip, Germany's VEBA AG, Austria's OMV and traders Taurus, MEES reported.
